description:
REQUIRES: opi-fin.6.1 (Host behaviour + Stub) and opi-fin.3.1 (Extension.Manager) merged first.

FILES: wherever OctoPi.Agent.start_session is implemented, api.ex

GOAL: Host behaviour is implemented by the coding agent process itself -- no separate Host.Server GenServer. The coding agent IS the host. ctx.host is the agent's own pid.

RATIONALE: A separate Host GenServer was considered but rejected. The coding agent already owns everything the Host needs to implement: the transport layer (for send_message), session state (for get_active_tools), abort capability. Adding a separate process creates coupling and coordination overhead with no benefit. The deadlock concern (handler calling back to a dispatching process) does not apply because the agent dispatches from a spawned Task, not from within its own GenServer callback.

WHAT THIS TICKET DOES:

STEP 1 -- Coding agent implements Host behaviour:
Add @behaviour OctoPi.Coder.Extension.Host to the coding agent module. Implement all Host callbacks: handle_call for queries (get_active_tools, get_model, etc.), handle_cast for fire-and-forget actions (send_message, append_entry, etc.).

STEP 2 -- Wire bind_core to use self():
In API.bind_core/2 (api.ex), add a :host_pid key. When the coding agent calls bind_core before loading extensions, it passes host_pid: self(). The generated fn-fields delegate to Host client functions:
  send_message: fn msg -> Host.send_message(host_pid, msg) end
  get_active_tools: fn -> Host.get_active_tools(host_pid) end
  etc.
Existing call sites passing individual fn values to bind_core continue to work unchanged.

STEP 3 -- Session startup sequence:
  {:ok, manager} = Extension.Manager.start_link(%{extension_paths: paths})  # linked
  ctx_base = %Context{
    host: self(),
    ui: ui_pid,
    handlers_table: Extension.Manager.table_refs(manager).handlers
  }
The agent holds the manager pid. All per-session infrastructure (Agents, ETS, Registry) lives under the Manager.

VALIDATION: Run full test suite. Zero extension tests should fail. Verify that Host.Stub (from opi-fin.6.1) can be used as a drop-in replacement for the coding agent pid in extension tests.
title: 6a: Introduce Host GenServer into session supervision tree
